title: `x-mcp-header`
description: A JSON Schema annotation that mirrors a primitive tool parameter into an `Mcp-Param-{name}` HTTP header when the tool is called over Streamable HTTP.
question: Does the client mirror annotated parameters into request headers, and reject tools that violate the constraints?
why: Servers use this so load balancers and proxies can route on a parameter without parsing the body. The spec requires Streamable HTTP clients to emit the header and to exclude tools whose annotation is malformed; a client that ignores the annotation breaks routing silently, with no error anyone can see.
known_issues: Measured by scripts/measure_protocol.py: each adapter runs against fixtures/base_protocol_server.py behind the wire recorder, and the cell is read from the captures.

notes.pydantic-ai: Pydantic AI: a direct `call_tool` sends `tools/call` before any `tools/list` in that request sequence, so it has not seen the `x-mcp-header` annotation and sends no `Mcp-Param-Region` header; the agent's call lists tools first and mirrors the parameter. The object-typed `bad_header` tool is excluded on both paths.
notes.copilot_sdk: GitHub Copilot SDK 1.0.19 (Copilot runtime 1.0.95): on Streamable HTTP the runtime mirrors an `x-mcp-header` parameter: the `routed_lookup` call sent `Mcp-Param-Region: eu-west-1`. The `bad_header` tool, which puts `x-mcp-header` on an object-typed parameter, is not excluded; it is offered to the model with the annotation still in its schema.
